meta.hypothesis: After ruling out sigma_exc/sigma_ion/excitation for the 23% cascade deficit, test the remaining lead: does the missing ionisation energy go to a non-ionising channel (vibrational or sub-cutoff thermalization)? Instrumented per-channel deposited energy via atomic counters in primary.wgsl + secondary.wgsl, read back through the native runtime.
meta.method: Added atomicAdd energy accumulators (counters[3]=E_exc, counters[6]=E_vib then E_subcutoff) to the deposit branches; ran native Phase A+B at 10 keV / 4096 primaries; read the counters buffer. Production shaders reverted after.

env.runner: local M2 Pro WebGPU via Deno

summary.headline: The energy budget is HEALTHY and ionisation-dominated (85%), just like Geant4. Excitation (730 eV, 73 events ~ Geant4 62.5), vibrational (100 eV, 1%), and sub-cutoff sec-thermalization (651 eV, 6.5%) are ALL small. The missing ~120 ions worth of energy does NOT go to a wrong channel.
summary.conclusion: The 23% cascade deficit / W-value 25.6-vs-19.6 is NOT an energy-misallocation. With sigma_exc (E7e), sigma_ion (sign), excitation, vibrational, and sub-cutoff all ruled out, the only remaining causes are: (a) a secondary-cascade ionisation-MULTIPLICATION shortfall (our ~40 eV secondaries re-ionise less than Geant4 on the way down), or (b) a COUNTING-CONVENTION difference (our H3O+ records vs Geant4 e-_G4DNAIonisation step count, incl. how autoionisation is tallied). Both need a Geant4 per-trackID / per-process re-analysis — Geant4-gated, not a quick check.
